clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10139 with a subject line describing an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute. The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer); this is not an until-date, so no inclusive or exclusive reading arises. The thirty-day report deadline and the statutory period after the report are not ends; the board reported on August 11, 1950 (held report title page), after which the order was functionally spent but remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10139 at 15 FR 4241, in the Federal Register of July 4, 1950 (PDF page 3; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The page header in the held text reads FEDERAL REGISTER 4241 with the date Tuesday, July 4, 1950; the order is headed Executive Order 10139 and is signed July 3, 1950. Its filing line in the text layer reads Filed, July 8, 1950, which cannot be right for a page published on July 4, 1950 and is read as an OCR error for July 3. The same page also prints Executive Order 10138, which concerns the Toledo, Lorain & Fairport Dock Company. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Toledo Lakefront Dock Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, Local 158, A. F. of L.; invoking section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, it states "I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate the said dispute." It provides that no member of the board may be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier, directs the board to report its findings to the President "within thirty days from the date of this order", and, as provided by section 10 of the Act, states that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board has reported "no change, except by agreement, shall be made" by the company or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the last operative sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10139 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10139_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10139_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_fe19979d2d.txt, PDF page 1) is titled as the report of the emergency board appointed July 3, 1950 by Executive Orders 10138 and 10139, and its title page is dated at Toledo, Ohio, August 11, 1950. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12553 revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in Federal Register text files of the same issue (the files for Executive Orders 10136 to 10139 hold the same pages) and a Federal Register codification guide for page 4241.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order without a saving clause, and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right; a bounded search of the held Executive Order 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR disposition notes shows no residual effect.
